theme: Common-gamma-chain cytokine signaling driving T and NK proliferation
story: The centre is IL-2 signaling through JAK-STAT5 (Interleukin-2 signaling, IL-2-mediated signaling, HALLMARK IL2-STAT5), joined by the other common-gamma-chain cytokines IL-7, IL-15 and IL-21 that share the same receptor subunit and JAK1/JAK3-STAT logic. IL-12 JAK-STAT signaling and the TCR network sit alongside as the activation context in which these cytokines act. The outputs are proliferation of activated T cells and proliferation and differentiation of NK cells, so the cluster as a whole describes cytokine-driven expansion and maintenance of lymphocytes.

theme: Scavenger receptor uptake of modified lipoproteins and foam cells
story: The core is scavenging by class A, B, F and H scavenger receptors, which bind and internalise modified ligands such as oxidised LDL. Lipoprotein particle signaling, cellular response to oxidised LDL, cholesterol storage and foam cell differentiation describe the consequence in macrophages: unregulated lipid uptake turns them into cholesterol-laden foam cells, the founding event of atherosclerotic plaques. Immune complex clearance and protein import reflect the broader clearance and internalisation role of the same receptors.

theme: tRNA charging and modification for accurate translation
story: The centre is tRNA aminoacylation in both cytosol and mitochondria, which loads each tRNA with its correct amino acid, together with translational fidelity processes that depend on correct charging and proofreading. Wobble-position modifications (uridine thiolation, guanine modification, t6A threonylcarbamoyladenosine) tune anticodon decoding, while tRNA intron splicing produces mature tRNAs. Selenocysteine synthesis on its tRNA and translational readthrough are special cases of decoding, so the cluster as a whole is about preparing tRNAs so the genetic code is read accurately.

theme: TLR adaptor signaling to NF-kB, IRF3/7 and cell death
story: The centre is the downstream signaling of Toll-like receptors: the TRIF (TICAM1) branch from TLR3/TLR4 and the MyD88-IRAK branch from TLR7/8/9, which converge on TRAF6, TAK1 and IKK complex recruitment. One output is NF-kB activation (regulated by SUMOylation and other controls), another is TBK1/IKKe-driven activation of IRF3 and IRF7 for interferon induction, and a third is RIP1- and TRIF-mediated programmed cell death, with ZBP1-RIP signaling joining the same RIP kinase node. Together the cluster describes how innate pathogen sensing at TLRs is converted into inflammatory, antiviral and cell-death responses.

theme: Pre-mRNA 3'-end processing, splicing and snRNP biogenesis
story: The core is mRNA 3'-end formation: co-transcriptional cleavage and polyadenylation, its coupling to RNA polymerase II termination, processing of intronless pre-mRNAs, and the special stem-loop/SLBP-dependent processing of replication-dependent histone mRNAs. The spliceosome and the biogenesis of its snRNPs (snRNP assembly, snRNA transport, cap hypermethylation) form the second arm, linked through positive regulation of splicing and 3'-end processing. Together the cluster describes nuclear maturation of RNA polymerase II transcripts into export-ready mRNAs.

theme: TCR signaling, costimulation and thymic T cell development
story: The centre is T cell receptor signaling: CD3/zeta phosphorylation, ZAP-70 recruitment to the immunological synapse and ITK/PKC signaling, amplified by CD28 costimulation through Vav1 and PI3K/Akt and restrained by CTLA4, BTLA and other negative regulators of TCR signaling. Thymic positive and negative selection, double-positive thymocytes and alpha-beta CD8 and gamma-delta differentiation show the same signals shaping T cell development, while the T cell module signatures mark the cell type. The cluster as a whole describes how TCR plus costimulatory and coinhibitory signals select, activate and differentiate T cells.

theme: Germ cell development and spermatogenesis
story: The cluster follows germline development from primordial germ cell migration and germ cell proliferation, through meiotic entry and telomere attachment to the nuclear envelope, to spermiogenesis structures such as the manchette and the sperm mitochondrial sheath. The Sertoli cell barrier and elimination of ectopic germ cells provide the supporting niche and quality control. TYSND1 cleavage of peroxisomal proteins and general cell maturation are peripheral, so the whole is mainly about producing mature male gametes.

theme: Oncogenic FLT3/PDGFR kinase signaling via STAT5 and CBL
story: The centre is signaling by class III receptor tyrosine kinases in haematopoiesis, especially FLT3 (ITD mutants, CBL mutants, SRC-family kinase signaling) and PDGFRA/B mutants and fusions, with cytosolic FGFR1 fusions alongside. STAT5 activation is the shared downstream output, also used by thrombopoietin and G-CSF receptor signaling, while CBL-mediated ubiquitination and negative regulation of FLT3 and CSF3 signaling act as the brake. Together the cluster describes cytokine-receptor kinase signaling to STAT5 and how its constitutive activation by mutation drives myeloid leukaemias and related neoplasms.

theme: DNA double-strand break sensing and repair pathway choice
story: The centre is the response to double-strand breaks: sensing and ATM-mediated recruitment of repair proteins, followed by repair through homologous recombination (strand invasion, synthesis-dependent strand annealing, sister chromatid exchange) or through classical and alternative (MMEJ) non-homologous end joining. Positive and negative regulators of HR and NHEJ decide between these routes, while the BRCA1, BARD1 and BRCA2 defect pathways describe how losing HR factors breaks the response. Interstrand cross-link repair and repair DNA synthesis are related branches, so the cluster as a whole is about restoring broken chromosomes.

theme: Cation-chloride cotransport in cell volume and renal salt handling
story: The centre is the SLC12 cation-chloride cotransporters (NKCC, NCC, KCC), with Gitelman syndrome from SLC12A3 and corpus callosum agenesis with neuropathy from SLC12A6 as their disease forms. These cotransporters move Na+, K+ and Cl- together, which underlies renal sodium reabsorption and transepithelial chloride transport, and also cell volume regulation through hyperosmotic and hypotonic responses and osmosensory signaling. Regulation of sodium and potassium transport and intracellular anion homeostasis complete the picture of coupled salt and water balance at the cell and epithelial level.

theme: mRNA 3'-end processing and cytoplasmic mRNA decay
story: The cluster spans an mRNA's life from 3'-end formation to destruction. Nuclear cleavage, polyadenylation, termination and histone mRNA stem-loop processing make the 3' end, while deadenylation, decapping, 5'-to-3' exonucleolytic decay, P-body assembly and miRNA-mediated destabilization remove the message. Poly(A) tail regulation and 3'-UTR-mediated stabilization link the two ends, so the cluster as a whole describes how the poly(A) tail and cap set mRNA stability and turnover.

theme: Amino acid biosynthesis and catabolism, one-carbon related
story: The cluster is general amino acid metabolism, with many umbrella terms for L-amino acid synthesis and breakdown. Specific routes include histidine and proline catabolism, proline, glycine and aspartate-family biosynthesis, and glyoxylate and formate metabolism, which connect glycine and serine to one-carbon units. It is a broad metabolic grouping held together by nitrogen and carbon handling of amino acids rather than one pathway.

theme: COPI retrograde Golgi-to-ER vesicle traffic
story: The centre is COPI-coated vesicle budding and COPI-dependent Golgi-to-ER retrograde traffic, which return escaped ER proteins and recycle trafficking machinery. The obsolete vesicle-targeting terms and localization to ER exit sites describe the targeting steps of the same early secretory pathway between ER and Golgi. Together the cluster describes vesicle traffic at the ER-Golgi interface.

theme: Base excision repair and direct reversal of DNA damage
story: The centre is base excision repair: DNA glycosylases (OGG1, MUTYH, NTHL1, NEIL1) remove damaged bases, APEX1 handles the abasic site, and short-patch or POLB/PCNA-dependent long-patch synthesis fills the gap. The many defect pathways describe disease-causing loss of glycosylase binding or processing. Direct reversal of alkylation damage by MGMT, ALKBH2 and ALKBH3 is a parallel repair route, and CpG island demethylation reflects the use of BER (TDG) in active DNA demethylation, so the cluster as a whole is about repairing small chemical lesions on DNA bases.

theme: Axon guidance, sprouting and Sema3A repulsion
story: The centre is semaphorin 3A signaling through plexins, CRMPs, PAK and integrin inhibition, which repels growth cones and limits axon extension and microtubule polymerization. Positive and negative regulation of collateral sprouting, sprouting of injured axons and regulation of neuron projection regeneration describe the same growth and repulsion control in plasticity and injury. Peripheral nervous system development, dorsal root ganglion and sympathetic neuron projection outgrowth, nerve branching and innervation set the developmental context, so the cluster as a whole is about steering and limiting axon growth.

theme: Insulin/IGF receptor signaling through RAS and PI3K-AKT
story: The cluster centres on receptor tyrosine kinase signaling from IGF1R and insulin receptor substrates: IRS activation and SHC/SOS events feed RAS, while PI3K activates AKT, including AKT2. AKT outputs include TSC complex inhibition (toward mTOR) and glycogen synthesis, while PP2A/IER3, RAS GAPs and signal attenuation provide negative control. The cancer-related pathways (aberrant PI3K, NF1 loss, RAS GAP and RAS mutants) show the same RAS and PI3K-AKT axis turned on constitutively in disease.

theme: Non-vesicular phospholipid transfer at ER membrane contacts
story: The centre is intermembrane lipid transfer: phosphatidylinositol and phosphatidylcholine are moved from the ER to the Golgi and other membranes by lipid transfer proteins rather than vesicles. PI synthesis in the ER supplies the cargo, and ER-plasma membrane tethering and ER localization describe the membrane contact sites where transfer happens. Together it describes how the ER distributes phospholipids to other organelles.

theme: Mammary gland development and lactation
story: The cluster follows the mammary gland from thelarche and ductal elongation and branching, through pregnancy-associated branching and alveolar development, to epithelial differentiation and lactation. Epithelial proliferation and the alveolar cell developmental lineage are the cellular engines of this growth. Together it describes how the mammary epithelium is built and matured for milk production.

theme: Centrosome, centriole and microtubule organization with cilia
story: The centre is the centrosome as microtubule-organizing centre: centriole duplication, elongation and cohesion, microtubule nucleation and anchoring, and positioning of the centrosome. Tubulin polyglutamylation and deglutamylation, microtubule severing and regulators of microtubule polymerization and depolymerization tune microtubule stability. Basal body docking, cilium assembly and disassembly show the centriole's second role as ciliary basal body, so the cluster as a whole is about building and regulating the microtubule cytoskeleton from centrosome and cilium.

theme: Stress-induced senescence and p53 damage response
story: The cluster is about cellular responses to genotoxic and oxidative stress, especially UV (HALLMARK UV up and down, UV-B response). Oxidative stress-induced and stress-induced premature senescence and reduced fibroblast proliferation are one outcome. Negative regulation of p53-mediated apoptosis, the DNA damage response and stress kinase signaling describes the brakes that decide between survival, arrest and death.

theme: Chemokine-directed leukocyte migration and lymphoid tissue organization
story: The centre is chemokines and their receptors (chemokine clusters, CCR1/7, CXCL12-CXCR4) and the chemotaxis they drive in T, B, NK, dendritic, mast and myeloid cells, with S1P receptor, Rac and Cdc42 signaling and pseudopodium assembly providing the migration machinery. Homing into lymph nodes and gut- and mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue, and lymph node development, show chemokines organizing lymphoid organs, while B cell, dendritic cell and monocyte differentiation and the myeloid and mesenchymal BTM modules supply cell types that respond. Together the cluster describes how chemokine gradients position immune cells in tissue and lymphoid organs.

theme: Complement cascade activation and its regulation
story: The centre is the complement system: classical antibody-triggered activation, the alternative pathway and the terminal pathway assembling the membrane attack complex. Many members are regulators that promote or restrain activation, limit MAC assembly and protect host cells from complement-dependent cytotoxicity. Together the cluster describes humoral innate defence through complement and the controls that prevent damage to self.

theme: Neutrophil and myeloid recruitment by chemokines and formyl peptides
story: The centre is recruitment of neutrophils and other myeloid cells: formyl peptide receptors sensing bacterial and damage-derived formyl peptides, G protein coupled receptors, and regulation of granulocyte, neutrophil and macrophage chemotaxis. The production of CXCL1, CXCL2, CCL2, CCL3 and CCL5 supplies the chemokine signals, and the neutrophil module marks the responding cells. Together it describes the early inflammatory recruitment of phagocytes to sites of infection or injury.

theme: COPII and COPI vesicle traffic between ER and Golgi
story: The centre is the early secretory pathway: COPII vesicles load cargo at ER exit sites and carry it to the Golgi, while COPI vesicles mediate intra-Golgi and retrograde Golgi-to-ER traffic. Vesicle tethering and targeting terms, cargo concentration in the ER and regulation of ER-to-Golgi transport describe the steps that ensure correct delivery. Together the cluster describes the bidirectional vesicle shuttle that moves secretory proteins out of the ER and recycles machinery back.

theme: Phospholipid and glycolipid transfer and membrane flipping
story: The centre is movement of lipids between and within membranes: intermembrane transfer of PI and PC from ER to Golgi, glycolipid, glycosphingolipid and ceramide-1-phosphate transport, and P4-ATPase flippase translocation of aminophospholipids such as phosphatidylserine across the bilayer. PI synthesis supplies the cargo, and regulation of phospholipid transport and translocation completes the core. The BTM modules connect this lipid handling to vesicle traffic and flippase machinery, so the cluster describes how cells set membrane lipid composition and asymmetry.

theme: Phagocytic clearance of apoptotic cells, amyloid and lipoproteins
story: The centre is clearance by macrophages and microglia: recognition and engulfment of apoptotic cells via exposed phosphatidylserine, neutrophil clearance, and scavenger receptor uptake via class A, B, F and H receptors. Amyloid-beta clearance and microglial activation and differentiation extend this to the brain, while uptake of oxidised LDL, cholesterol storage and foam cell formation show the lipid-loading side of the same receptors. Together the cluster describes how professional phagocytes remove dying cells and debris, and how this goes wrong in atherosclerosis and neurodegeneration.

theme: Excitatory amino acid and glycine transporters at synapses
story: The centre is glutamate reuptake by the SLC1 excitatory amino acid transporters, which also carry L- and D-aspartate and keep extracellular glutamate low, including astrocytic uptake and the glutamate-glutamine cycle. Glycinergic transmission with the GlyT2 transporter SLC6A5 and vesicular glutamate loading by SLC17A8 add other parts of neurotransmitter handling. Disease pathways for SLC1A1, SLC1A3, SLC6A5 and SLC17A8 (schizophrenia, episodic ataxia, hyperekplexia, deafness) show what happens when this transport fails.

theme: Heart morphogenesis: chambers, septa, valves and outflow
story: The cluster describes building the heart. Ventricle and atrial formation with trabecular and compact myocardium and cardiomyocyte differentiation form the muscular core, from second heart field progenitor proliferation onward. Endocardial cushion formation by epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition gives rise to the septa and the mitral, tricuspid, aortic and pulmonary valves, while outflow and coronary vessel development (pulmonary artery, ascending aorta) complete the organ.

theme: Myelination, glial responses and axon regeneration control
story: The cluster combines myelin and glial biology with axon regrowth. One arm is myelination by oligodendrocytes in the CNS and Schwann cells in the PNS (EGR2/SOX10 initiation, LGI-ADAM interactions, myelin maintenance, OPC proliferation, negative regulation of myelination). The other arm is axon sprouting and regeneration with stimulation and RHOA-driven inhibition of axonal growth, linked through reactive gliosis and ceramide signaling, which is how glia and myelin-derived signals restrict or allow repair after injury.

theme: Base excision repair of damaged bases and single-strand breaks
story: The centre is base excision repair: DNA glycosylases recognise and cleave damaged purines and pyrimidines, the abasic site is processed, and the gap is filled by short-patch or POLB/PCNA-dependent long-patch synthesis. Single-strand break repair is the shared downstream step. NEIL1 and NEIL3 defects and NEIL3-mediated resolution of interstrand cross-links extend the same glycosylases to disease and cross-link repair, so the cluster is about removing small base lesions from DNA.

theme: Erythrocyte gas exchange and Rh membrane proteins
story: The centre is red blood cell gas transport: erythrocytes take up oxygen and release CO2 in the lungs and do the reverse in tissues, with intracellular oxygen transport and nitric oxide transport by haemoglobin. Rh blood group biosynthesis and Rh-null anaemia from RHAG defects add the erythrocyte membrane proteins (including the RhAG gas channel), and the membrane and transport modules capture the same red cell membrane programme. Together it describes the red cell as a gas-exchange cell.

theme: Lung development: branching, mesenchyme and vasculature
story: The centre is lung morphogenesis: bud elongation and regulated branching, lobe formation and overall lung growth. Mesenchymal proliferation and lung-associated mesenchyme development provide the signals and tissue that drive epithelial branching, and lung vasculature development builds the vessels. Diaphragm development and ductus arteriosus closure belong to the same respiratory and perinatal transition to air breathing.

theme: Embryonic axial patterning: neural plate, hindbrain and limbs
story: The cluster is about early embryonic body patterning. Anterior and posterior neural plate formation, neural plate border and neural crest specification, and midbrain-hindbrain and rhombomere development pattern the nervous system, with anterior HOX activation setting hindbrain identity. Dorsal-ventral axis specification, anatomical boundary formation, anterior-posterior body region determination and forelimb, hindlimb and digit morphogenesis apply the same signal-driven gene regulation to the trunk and limbs.

theme: Eye development: retina, lens and anterior structures
story: The cluster describes building the camera-type eye. Optic cup and embryonic retina morphogenesis, retinal layering and photoreceptor and amacrine differentiation form the neural retina, with retinal ganglion cell axon guidance and optic nerve formation connecting it to the brain. Lens fibre morphogenesis and transparency (with gap junction transport), cornea, iris, eyelid and pigmentation complete the anterior eye.

theme: Osteoclast differentiation, fusion and bone resorption
story: The centre is the osteoclast: positive and negative regulation of osteoclast differentiation and proliferation, DAP12 (TYROBP) signaling that drives it, and fusion of macrophage-lineage precursors into multinucleated cells (macrophage fusion, syncytium and membrane fusion). The output is bone resorption and its control within bone remodeling. Together it describes how bone-resorbing cells are formed and regulated.

theme: Cellular responses to heavy and trace metals
story: The centre is metal detoxification: MTF1 activates metallothionein genes, and metallothioneins bind zinc, copper, cadmium and other metals. Responses to zinc, copper, manganese, iron, cobalt, selenium, lead and mercury are the stimuli that engage this system. Chaperone-mediated autophagy regulation is peripheral, so the cluster as a whole is about sensing and buffering metal ions.

theme: RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK signaling, oncogenic mutants and feedback
story: The centre is the MAPK cascade: RAF activation, MAP2K and MAPK activation and RSK as an ERK output, with SHOC2-MRAS complexes promoting RAF. A large group describes oncogenic activation by RAS, BRAF (including paradoxical activation by kinase-dead BRAF), RAF1, MAP2K and MAPK mutants, fusions and NF1 loss. Negative feedback, ERK inactivation and dual-specificity phosphatase dephosphorylation provide the brakes, so the cluster is about how ERK signaling is driven, deregulated in cancer and RASopathies, and switched off.

theme: E2F-driven DNA replication and cell cycle proliferation
story: The centre is DNA replication in the mitotic cell cycle: origin initiation, DNA unwinding and replication, and regulation of polymerase activity. E2F1 targets and the G1/S transition describe the transcriptional switch that turns on the replication genes, and cell cycle and cell division modules mark proliferating cells. Break-induced replication and negative regulation of replication add control of replication stress, so the cluster as a whole describes the proliferation programme of S phase.

theme: Cellular senescence: arrest, Polycomb silencing and SASP
story: The centre is cellular senescence: oncogene-induced senescence, positive regulation of senescence and blocked G0-to-G1 re-entry describe stable proliferative arrest. Polycomb repression by BMI1 and its opposition by USP16 control the CDKN2A locus, and TFAP2 regulation of cell cycle factors adds transcriptional control. The senescence-associated secretory phenotype is the inflammatory output, so the cluster describes how cells enter senescence and what they secrete.

theme: Platelet activation by GPCR agonists and cytoskeleton
story: The centre is platelet activation through G protein coupled receptors: thrombin via PARs, ADP via P2Y1 and P2Y12, and thromboxane via TP. Prostacyclin signaling through its receptor provides the opposing inhibitory signal, and LDL sensitization adds a lipid modulator. Platelet activation modules, actin binding and integrin-talin cytoskeletal remodeling describe the shape change and adhesion that follow, so the cluster describes how platelets are switched on for haemostasis.

theme: Dendritic cell and monocyte antigen-presenting surface programs
story: The centre is antigen presentation by dendritic cells and monocytes: surface signatures of resting, LPS-activated and general DCs and monocytes, CD1 lipid antigen presentation by MHC class Ib, and regulation of DC differentiation and antigen processing. Butyrophilin interactions, T cell and Th1 surface signatures and plasma cell signatures represent the lymphocytes these cells engage. Together the cluster describes the cell identity and surface receptor repertoire of myeloid antigen-presenting cells.

theme: B cell activation, germinal centres and plasma cell differentiation
story: The centre is the B cell lineage as captured by surface and module signatures for naive, memory and total B cells. Germinal centre B cell differentiation, T follicular helper differentiation, ICOS and CD27 costimulation and BCR signaling describe the T-B interaction that drives affinity maturation. Plasma cell differentiation and immunoglobulin modules and adaptive memory are the outputs, so the cluster describes the humoral response from B cell activation to antibody-secreting and memory cells.

theme: Lysosomal glycolipid and glycan catabolism and its disorders
story: The centre is lysosomal breakdown of glycoconjugates: glycosphingolipid and ganglioside catabolism and lysosomal oligosaccharide catabolism by hexosaminidases and neuraminidase. Their defects (HEXA and HEXB in GM2 gangliosidoses, NEU1 in sialidosis) are lysosomal storage diseases. N-glycan processing in the ER (MOGS, MAN1B1) and its congenital disorders are the biosynthetic side of the same glycan trimming, so the cluster describes processing and degradation of glycans.

theme: Regulation of T helper and regulatory T cell responses
story: The cluster centres on control of T cell effector function: regulatory T cell differentiation, Th1 and Th17 commitment and CD4 and CD8 activation and proliferation. Most members are negative regulators, limiting IL-2, IL-21 and interferon-gamma production and T cell proliferation, with positive regulation of Treg and Th1 differentiation as counterweights. Together it describes how the balance between effector and regulatory T cells is set to maintain tolerance.

theme: tRNA processing and modification in nucleus and mitochondria
story: The centre is maturation of tRNA precursors: 5'-leader removal by RNase P, 3'-end processing and intron splicing in the nucleus, and the parallel processing and modification of mitochondrial tRNAs and other mitochondrial RNA 3' ends. tRNA-derived small RNA biogenesis is a further product of tRNA cleavage. Together the cluster describes how functional tRNAs are made in both genetic compartments.

theme: Notch receptor signaling to nuclear transcription
story: The centre is Notch signaling: ligand-induced cleavage of NOTCH1, 2, 3 and 4 releases the intracellular domain, which travels to the nucleus and activates targets such as HES/HEY (Notch-HLH pathway, Hallmark Notch). Constitutive NOTCH1 signaling by HD-domain and translocation mutants describes its oncogenic activation in T-ALL, and negative regulation of the pathway provides control. Together it is a compact picture of Notch-driven transcription.

theme: Meiotic recombination, synapsis and chromosome segregation
story: The centre is meiotic recombination: programmed double-strand break formation, strand invasion and repair, synaptonemal complex assembly and synapsis, crossover and chiasma formation and resolution of intermediates. Sister chromatid cohesion, telomere attachment to the nuclear envelope and meiotic checkpoints support this, and spindle assembly, chromosome alignment and segregation in male and female meiosis I use the chiasmata. Together it describes how homologous chromosomes pair, recombine and separate to make haploid gametes.

theme: TNFR1-driven NF-kB signaling and ubiquitin regulation
story: The centre is TNF receptor 1 signaling to canonical NF-kB, with TNFR1-induced apoptosis as the alternative outcome. Linear polyubiquitination (LUBAC), deubiquitination and SUMOylation regulate the signaling complex and decide between survival and death. Many generic terms for positive and negative regulation of NF-kB and transcription factor activity frame the same pathway, so the cluster describes how inflammatory TNF signals are turned into NF-kB-driven gene expression.

theme: Coronavirus replication and host translation control
story: The centre is SARS-CoV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 genome replication: translation of the replicase by ribosomal frameshifting, maturation of the replicase proteins and assembly of the replication-transcription complex, with viral cap methylation to evade IFIT. The viruses' modulation of host translation and host-mediated suppression of viral replication show the conflict over translation machinery, and L13a-mediated silencing and inhibition of elongation are host translational controls. Together it describes how coronaviruses take over translation to replicate and how the host pushes back.

theme: Cytosolic nucleic acid sensing to IRF3/7 type I interferon
story: The centre is induction of type I interferon: RIG-I and MDA5 sensing of viral RNA and TLR3 and TLR7/8/9 signaling converge on TBK1/IKKe activation of IRF3 and IRF7. Their output is interferon-alpha and -beta production and type I interferon signaling, while negative regulators of RIG-I/MDA5 keep the response in check. Together it describes the antiviral innate alarm triggered by foreign double-stranded RNA.
